sigiriya.name: Sigiriya
sigiriya.shortDescription: Climb the legendary Lion Rock fortress rising 200 m above the jungle — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Sri Lanka's most iconic landmark.
sigiriya.longDescription: Sigiriya, known as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World', is a spectacular ancient rock fortress and palace ruin built in the 5th century AD. The site rises dramatically from the surrounding flat plains and features ancient frescoes, the famous Mirror Wall, and elaborate water gardens at the base. Climbing to the summit rewards visitors with panoramic views across the jungle canopy and reveals the story of King Kashyapa who ruled here for 18 years.

temple-of-the-tooth.name: Temple of the Tooth
temple-of-the-tooth.shortDescription: Sri Lanka's most revered Buddhist shrine, home to the sacred tooth relic of the Buddha, set beside the serene Kandy Lake.
temple-of-the-tooth.longDescription: The Sri Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic) in Kandy is one of the most sacred places in the Buddhist world. The temple houses the relic of the tooth of the Buddha, which has been an object of veneration since the 4th century AD. The golden-roofed complex is the cultural heart of Kandy and hosts the spectacular Esala Perahera festival each August. The surrounding Kandy city with its botanical gardens and lake adds to the magical atmosphere.

galle-fort.name: Galle Fort
galle-fort.shortDescription: A perfectly preserved Dutch colonial fortified city on the southern tip of Sri Lanka — narrow streets, boutique cafes, and ocean views from the ramparts.
galle-fort.longDescription: Galle Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site built by the Portuguese in the 16th century and extensively fortified by the Dutch during the 17th century. The fort is a remarkable example of an urban ensemble illustrating the interaction of European architecture and South Asian traditions. Walking the ancient ramparts at sunset, exploring the lighthouse, colourful churches, mosques, and boutique shops within the fort walls is a uniquely atmospheric experience.

ella-nine-arches.name: Ella & Nine Arches Bridge
ella-nine-arches.shortDescription: A charming highland village perched at 1,000 m with the iconic Nine Arches Bridge, Little Adam's Peak hike, and the world's most scenic train ride.
ella-nine-arches.longDescription: Ella is a small town in the Badulla District, nestled among rolling tea estates and misty mountains. The famous Nine Arches Bridge is a colonial-era marvel of stone and brick with no metal used in its construction. Visitors come to watch the blue train glide over the bridge at sunset — one of Sri Lanka's most photographed moments. The surrounding area offers hikes to Little Adam's Peak, Ella Rock, and Ravana Falls.

yala-national-park.name: Yala National Park
yala-national-park.shortDescription: The highest density of leopards in the world, alongside elephants, sloth bears, and hundreds of bird species in a dramatic landscape of jungle and lagoon.
yala-national-park.longDescription: Yala National Park is Sri Lanka's most visited and second largest national park, covering 979 square kilometres of forest, grassland, and lagoon. It is famous for having one of the world's highest densities of leopards, making leopard sightings relatively common. The park is also home to elephants, water buffalo, sloth bears, mugger crocodiles, and an extraordinary diversity of bird life. Dawn and dusk jeep safaris are the best way to explore this extraordinary wilderness.

nuwara-eliya.name: Nuwara Eliya
nuwara-eliya.shortDescription: Sri Lanka's 'Little England' at 1,868 m — rolling tea estates, colonial Tudor architecture, cool mountain air, and the famous Victoria Park.
nuwara-eliya.longDescription: Nuwara Eliya, meaning 'City of Light', sits at the highest elevation in Sri Lanka and feels remarkably different from the tropical coast. British colonists built a hill station here in the 19th century, complete with red postboxes, Tudor-style hotels, a golf course, and manicured gardens. Today it is the heart of Sri Lanka's finest tea country. Gregory Lake, Hakgala Botanical Gardens, and the surrounding tea factory tours make it a fascinating stop on the Hill Country circuit.

mirissa.name: Mirissa
mirissa.shortDescription: A crescent bay of golden sand, coconut palms, and turquoise water — plus the best blue whale and dolphin watching in all of Asia.
mirissa.longDescription: Mirissa is a small fishing town on Sri Lanka's southern tip, known for its perfect crescent-shaped beach and world-class whale watching. Blue whales — the largest animals on Earth — pass close to shore from November to April, and Mirissa is considered one of the best places in the world to see them. The beach itself is ideal for swimming and snorkelling, and the sunset view from Parrot Rock is one of the most beautiful on the island.

dambulla-cave-temple.name: Dambulla Cave Temple
dambulla-cave-temple.shortDescription: Sri Lanka's largest and best-preserved cave temple complex with 153 Buddha statues and ancient murals covering 2,100 sq m of ceiling.
dambulla-cave-temple.longDescription: The Dambulla Cave Temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka. The five caves contain 153 Buddha statues, three statues of Sri Lankan kings, and four statues of gods and goddesses. The murals covering the ceilings and walls span 2,100 square metres and depict scenes from the life of the Buddha and legends from Sri Lankan history. The site has been a sacred place of pilgrimage for over 22 centuries.

anuradhapura.name: Anuradhapura
anuradhapura.shortDescription: Sri Lanka's first capital and one of the longest continuously inhabited cities in the world, home to towering ancient stupas and the sacred Bodhi tree.
anuradhapura.longDescription: Anuradhapura was the first capital of Sri Lanka and remained the political and religious capital for over 1,300 years. It is one of the eight UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Sri Lanka and contains some of the most impressive ancient monuments in Asia. The city is centred around the Sri Maha Bodhi — a sacred fig tree grown from a cutting of the original Bodhi tree under which the Buddha attained enlightenment, making it the oldest documented tree in human history. Towering dagobas (stupas) rise above the jungle canopy.

polonnaruwa.name: Polonnaruwa
polonnaruwa.shortDescription: Sri Lanka's medieval capital, boasting one of Asia's finest collections of 12th-century ruins — statues, moonstone steps, and royal palaces.
polonnaruwa.longDescription: Polonnaruwa was the second capital of Sri Lanka, reaching its zenith under King Parakramabahu I in the 12th century. The well-preserved ancient city contains a fascinating collection of ruins including the Royal Palace, Audience Hall, Gal Vihara (with its magnificent rock-cut Buddha sculptures), Rankot Vihara stupa, and the famous Parakrama Samudraya reservoir. The compact, bikeable ruins make Polonnaruwa one of the most enjoyable UNESCO sites in Sri Lanka to explore.
